coaching:
**Strengths:**

1.  Your engagement score (57/100) indicates some subtle torso/head movement, showing a foundation for more dynamic presentations. (Source: GestureLens - Temporal Distribution Analysis)
2. Smiling was detected, which helps connect with the audience.

**Areas to Improve:**

1.  Your posture score (2/100) falls significantly below the professional benchmark of 75-85%. Slouching more than 15% of the time reduces perceived credibility. (Source: Toastmasters International - Using Body Language Guide)
2.  Your gesture frequency (26.8/min) greatly exceeds the recommended 3-8 gestures per minute range, which may appear frantic. (Source: GestureLens: Visual Analysis of Gestures in Presentation Videos) Additionally, your gesture quality score (28/100) suggests over-reliance on one-handed or asymmetric gestures, which are less authoritative than bilateral gestures.
3. Your eye contact proxy (2/100) is considerably below the professional benchmark of 85-95%. Looking away more than 15% reduces perceived confidence. (Source: Overcoming Public Speaking Anxiety through Nonverbal Communication)

**Evidence-Based Technique:**

Stance strategy: When standing, distribute weight evenly on both feet, shoulder-width apart. When sitting, sit on front third of chair with feet flat on floor, spine straight but not rigid. This projects confidence and allows for natural movement. (Source: How to Improve Non-Verbal Communication Skills - Posture Strategies)
